text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali tells Malta Euro-Mediterranean conference of need for economic support to ensure regional balance.
- King Hassan sends condolence message to Saudi King Fahd on casualties of Mina fire.
- U.N. envoy in Western Sahara James Baker says he will do his best to break deadlock over referendum proceedings.
- James Baker says he has been assigned to assess situation in Western Sahara before finding best way to tackle crisis.
- Japanese group Nippon Electronic Company might cooperate with Morocco on telecommunications.
- French Lyonnaise des Eaux which is to take over Casablanca water and electricity distribution says there will be no price increase during first year and staff benefits will be preserved.
- State-owned airline Royal Air Maroc which posted a net profit of 145 million dirhams ($15.42 million) in 1996, expects to reach 270 million dirhams in 1997.
- Casablanca stock exchange seems to calm down after more than three months steady rise which is sign that excess of money on the market is being absorbed.
